title: The Passion Paradox
hook: Stop trying to "follow your passion." It is the worst piece of career advice you’ve ever received.
script:
(Visual: Text overlay "The Passion Paradox" over a shot of someone looking exhausted at a desk)
Narrator: We are told that passion is the fuel for success. But first-principles thinking suggests the opposite.
(Visual: Quick cut to a diagram showing Passion $\rightarrow$ Expectation $\rightarrow$ Disappointment)
Narrator: Passion is an emotion, and emotions are volatile. When you turn your passion into your paycheck, you don't just risk your income—you risk the thing you love.
(Visual: B-roll of a high-pressure corporate environment)
Narrator: The reality? Passion isn't the cause of mastery; it's the result of it. 
(Visual: Text pops up: Competence $\rightarrow$ Autonomy $\rightarrow$ Passion)
Narrator: You don't find a passion; you build a skill until you become so good at it that you start loving the power it gives you. Stop searching. Start building.
caption: Passion is a byproduct, not a prerequisite. The obsession with "finding your calling" often leads to paralysis or burnout. Shift your focus from seeking a feeling to building a rare and valuable skill set. Mastery creates passion, not the other way around. #RationalThoughts #FirstPrinciples #CareerStrategy #IndianProfessionals #PsychologyOfSuccess
